proof_summary: Set \(K_n=\lfloor\log_2 T_n\rfloor-1\); then the bit is determined by whether \(T_n\) lies below or above \(3\cdot2^{K_n}\), while the recurrence yields \(1.83\le T_{n+1}/T_n\le 923/500\) and makes each \(K_n\) increase by at most one. Exhausting these possible exponent increments with the ratio bounds and Tribonacci recurrence forces at least three further zeros after a \(1\to0\) transition and two further ones after a \(0\to1\) transition, but excludes six consecutive zeros and five consecutive ones; direct computation handles run starts below 25.
